title: Broccoli Nutrient Deficiency: Signs, Causes and the Fertilizer That Fixes It
metaTitle: Broccoli Nutrient Deficiency: Signs and Fertilizer Fix
metaDescription: Broccoli nutrient deficiency shows in the leaves. See the signs of nitrogen, boron and calcium in brokoli, how to be sure, and the fertilizer to apply.
excerpt: Broccoli nutrient deficiency is one of the first things to check when the leaves of your brokoli (broccoli) turn yellow, purple or burnt at the edges. On Philippine farms the usual ones are nitrogen, boron, calcium, potassium, phosphorus, magnesium, sulfur and molybdenum. This guide shows where each one starts, how to be sure, and the fertilizer that fixes it.

heroImage.alt: Boron deficiency on a leaf, shown on another crop as a stand in for broccoli

blocks.text: Start with one question: did the change begin on the old leaves or on the young ones? Nitrogen, potassium, phosphorus, magnesium and molybdenum move inside the plant, so a shortage shows on the old, lower leaves first. But boron, calcium and sulfur stay where the plant first put them, so the young leaves and the growing tip show it first. After that, the color and the pattern narrow down which broccoli nutrient deficiency you have, and a soil test confirms it. Each one below has its signs, its causes and its fix.

blocks.text: Before you buy fertilizer for a broccoli nutrient deficiency

So use the table to pick the likeliest broccoli nutrient deficiency, then read its section below. Also keep in mind that dry soil, standing water, cold nights, a pest or a disease can look the same. That is why it pays to check the roots and the whole field first.
Nitrogen deficiency in broccoli

Leaves and heads turn evenly pale, starting on older leaves. Mature leaves yellow with orange to red color along the edges. Heads are small and loose, or do not form at all in severe cases. Plants are stunted and slow, with a higher risk of early bolting. You see it most at this stage: early leaf growth and again as the florets form. Broccoli needs nitrogen early, then a moderate supply at heading.
Why nitrogen deficiency happens in brokoli
Sandy soils, heavy rain or irrigation, low organic matter, raw straw or manure. A single unsplit dose that runs out before heading.
How to tell it apart
Red leaf edges can also come from phosphorus shortage. Phosphorus leaves are dark or bluish, nitrogen leaves are pale. To be sure, soil test and leaf tissue test.
What to apply for nitrogen deficiency
Side dress urea or ammonium sulfate in split doses based on the soil test. For a quick green up, KAU suggests a urea spray at 10 grams per liter of water every 15 days for cole crops such as cabbage.

Sold here with nitrogen: **Atlas Granular Urea** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (46 0 0), **YaraVera Viking Ship Granular Urea** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (46 0 0), **Planters Products Granular Urea** by Planters Products, Inc. (46 0 0) and **Harbest Granular Urea** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (46 0 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [urea fertilizer](/blog/urea-fertilizer), and the page on [nitrogen deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/nitrogen-deficiency) in every crop. In anee.io, Anee, the [smart farm technician](/features/ai-agricultural-technician), reads a photo of the leaf and tells you which nutrient is short.
To keep it away, give nitrogen early after transplanting and a second dose before heading.
Boron deficiency in broccoli

Watery tissue forms inside the stem and slowly turns brown or black, then dries out and leaves a hollow with brown patches. New leaves look crinkled and mottled, and plants are stunted with short spaces between leaves. Light brown spots can show on the head, and soft rot bacteria may enter the hollow stem. You see it most at this stage: head formation.
Why boron deficiency happens in brokoli
High soil pH, sandy soils where boron leaches, low organic matter, high nitrogen or calcium, drought or cold wet weather. Crucifers need more boron than most crops.
How to tell it apart
Hollowness from excess nitrogen or heat stays bright inside instead of browning. To be sure, cut stems lengthwise. Soil test and leaf tissue test for boron.
What to apply for boron deficiency

Delaware extension advises about 3 pounds of boron per acre in the fertilizer before planting for broccoli, or a spray of 1.0 to 1.5 pounds of Solubor per acre in plenty of water before heading if no boron went in the soil. For cole crops, KAU gives borax at about 10 kg per hectare in the soil or a 1 gram per liter spray. Do not overdo it. Too much boron burns leaf edges.

Sold here with boron: **Solubor** by Caldic Philippines Inc. (21 percent boron), **Etifert 11 (Borax Decahydrate)** by Zetryl.Chem Phils., Inc. (11 percent boron), **YaraVita BORTRAC 150** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (11.1 percent boron) and **Grow More Liquid Chelate Boron** by Sagrex Corporation (10 percent boron). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [boron deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/boron-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, include boron in the basal fertilizer on sandy or limed soils.
Calcium deficiency in broccoli
Young leaves are hit first, with dead lesions on the tips and edges that spread inward. Growth is restricted. You see it most at this stage: fast growth before and during heading.
Why calcium deficiency happens in brokoli
Restricted uptake more than low soil calcium: water stress, high ammonium, potassium, magnesium or sodium, and acid sandy soils.
How to tell it apart
Boron shortage also damages young leaves but brings hollow stems and crinkled leaves. To be sure, soil test for calcium, pH and boron.
What to apply for calcium deficiency

Keep the soil evenly moist. On acid soil, KAU suggests lime at about 250 kg per hectare when pH is 5.5 to 6, or about 840 kg per hectare in two doses when pH is 3.5 to 4.5. Gypsum on soil that is not acid.

Sold here with calcium: **Planters Products Lifelime** by Planters Products, Inc. (50.59 percent CaO), **Macrock Limestone** by Donumdei 1 Corp. (36 to 42 percent calcium), **Calcic Lime** by Mindanao Agriplus Corporation (35.52 percent calcium) and **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource Limited Corporation (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [fertilizer for tomatoes](/blog/fertilizer-for-tomatoes), and the page on [calcium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/calcium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, lime before planting, water evenly and avoid heavy ammonium and potash.
Potassium deficiency in broccoli

Older leaves turn yellow, then brown and dead, with a sharp border between dead and living tissue. The damage spreads from the edges inward, and in severe cases growth is badly stunted. Heads are smaller and of lower quality. You see it most at this stage: head formation and head enlargement, when broccoli needs the most potassium.
Why potassium deficiency happens in brokoli
Acid or sandy soils, heavy rain or irrigation, drought, low potassium reserves and soils rich in magnesium.
How to tell it apart
Magnesium shortage yellows between the veins first. Potassium burns the edges. To be sure, soil test for potassium and a leaf tissue test.
What to apply for potassium deficiency

Apply muriate of potash based on the soil test, in split doses before and at heading. For an immediate remedy on cole crops, KAU suggests a morning spray of sulfate of potash at 10 grams per liter of water with a sticker.

Sold here with potassium: **Atlas Muriate of Potash** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Philphos Muriate of Potash** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Harbest Granular Muriate of Potash** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (0 0 60) and **Swire Muriate of Potash** by Swire Agrotech Agricultural Products Inc. (0 0 60). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [potash fertilizer](/blog/potash-fertilizer), and the page on [potassium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/potassium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, give potash before head formation.
Phosphorus deficiency in broccoli

Older leaves turn reddish starting at the edges, with a yellow green band between the red and the green. Early on leaf size is normal. In severe cases leaves and the whole plant stay small. You see it most at this stage: early growth, most often in cold soils or drought.
Why phosphorus deficiency happens in brokoli
Cold soils and drought, acid or calcareous soils, iron rich soils, low organic matter and weak roots. Broccoli is more sensitive to low phosphorus than cabbage or cauliflower.
How to tell it apart
Nitrogen shortage also reddens leaf edges but the leaves are pale overall. To be sure, soil test for available phosphorus and pH.
What to apply for phosphorus deficiency
Apply phosphorus near the roots based on the soil test. For cole crops KAU lists single superphosphate for a quick fix and rock phosphate or bone meal for the long term.

Sold here with phosphorus: **Triple Super Phosphate** by Newman Chemicals Corporation (0 46 0), **Sagrex Duofos Granular Guano Phosphate** by Sagrex Corporation (0 22 0 (guano phosphate)), **Philphos 18 46 0** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0 (diammonium phosphate)) and **Atlas Di Ammonium Phosphate** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [16 20 0 fertilizer](/blog/16-20-0-fertilizer), and the page on [phosphorus deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/phosphorus-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, use a phosphorus starter at transplanting.
Magnesium deficiency in broccoli

Yellowing starts on older leaves and spreads between the veins from the edges inward. While the veins stay green and the leaf looks mottled. Severe cases get dead spots between the veins and along the edges, and growth is stunted. You see it most at this stage: head formation.
Why magnesium deficiency happens in brokoli
Excess potassium, ammonium or calcium, sandy or acid soils, heavy potash fertilizer, and cold wet periods.
How to tell it apart
Potassium shortage can look similar. Magnesium usually yellows the whole area between veins before dead spots appear. To be sure, leaf tissue test plus soil test for magnesium and potassium.
What to apply for magnesium deficiency
For cole crops KAU suggests magnesium sulfate in a band near the plants at about 80 kg per hectare (32 kg per acre). A foliar spray of magnesium sulfate gives faster relief.

Sold here with magnesium: **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource Limited Corporation (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium), **YaraTera KRISTA MgS** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (16 percent MgO and 13 percent sulfur), **Magnepro** by Ramgo International Corporation (16 percent MgO and 12.8 percent sulfur) and **Lucky Planters Magnesium Sulphate Heptahydrate (Epsom Salt)** by Mindanao Agriplus Corporation (16.27 percent MgO and 13 percent sulfur). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [complete fertilizer](/blog/complete-fertilizer-14-14-14), and the page on [magnesium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/magnesium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, use dolomite on acid soil.
Sulfur deficiency in broccoli

Yellowing starts in the youngest leaves, first between the veins and later evenly pale. Stems, leaf stalks and leaves may turn purple. Leaves become stiff, curl inward and grow narrow and spoon shaped on long stalks. Severe cases are badly stunted. You see it most at this stage: early growth.
Why sulfur deficiency happens in brokoli
Acid or sandy soils, low organic matter, waterlogged soils, and very high nitrogen, which can hold back sulfur uptake.
How to tell it apart
Nitrogen shortage starts on old leaves. Magnesium shortage also yellows between veins but on old leaves. To be sure, soil test for sulfate and a leaf tissue test.
What to apply for sulfur deficiency
Use ammonium sulfate as part of the nitrogen. For cole crops, KAU suggests sulfur dust at about 25 kg per hectare (10 kg per acre) on sulfur deficient soil.

Sold here with sulfur: **Farmfix Sulfur** by Philippine FarmFix, Inc. (99 percent sulfur), **VSI Sulfur Powder** by Newman Chemicals Corporation (99.5 percent sulfur), **Atlas Ammosul** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (21 0 0 with 24 percent sulfur) and **Philphos 21 0 0** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (21 0 0 (ammonium sulfate)). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [ammonium sulfate fertilizer](/blog/ammonium-sulfate-21-0-0), and the page on [sulfur deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/sulfur-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, give some sulfur every crop.
Molybdenum deficiency in broccoli

Leaves stay pale and the plant is stunted, with yellow green color between the veins and along the edges. Young leaves are narrow and distorted with edges that cup up or scorch, similar to whiptail in cauliflower. Affected plants usually come in patches. You see it most at this stage: seedling and young plant stage.
Why molybdenum deficiency happens in brokoli
Acid soils, mostly pH 5.5 or lower, and low organic matter.
How to tell it apart

Boron shortage also distorts young leaves. Nitrogen shortage gives pale plants without distorted leaves. To be sure, soil pH test. NSW DPI suggests a trial spray of sodium molybdate on a few plants and checking for greener, normal new growth.
What to apply for molybdenum deficiency

NSW DPI suggests about 50 grams of sodium molybdate in 100 liters of water sprayed on the leaves, or 150 ml of that mix at the base of each plant. For the next crop, mix about 1 kg sodium molybdate per hectare with the fertilizer, or treat the seedbed with 40 grams in 50 liters per 10 square meters one to two weeks before transplanting.

Sold here with molybdenum: **Tierramino Molybdenum** by Unilox Far East Resources Inc. (16 percent molybdenum), **YaraVita Teprosyn Mo** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (15 percent P2O5 and 15.3 percent molybdenum), **Biozome** by Manchem Industries, Inc. (12 percent S, 12 percent Zn, 3 percent Mn, 1 percent Mg, 1 percent Fe, 1 percent Cu, 0.5 percent B, 0.05 percent Mo) and **Grow More Liquid Chelate General Purpose** by Sagrex Corporation (2 percent Fe, 0.5 percent Mn, 1 percent Mg, 3 percent S with Cu, Zn, B, Mo). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [molybdenum deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/molybdenum-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, lime acid soils to about pH 6 ahead of planting.

blocks.title: Let a soil test decide the rate
blocks.text: A soil test is the surest check for any broccoli nutrient deficiency. Before you buy, ask your Municipal Agriculture Office where to send a soil sample. The DA regional soil laboratories and the Bureau of Soils and Water Management test soil, and the result says how much of each fertilizer your brokoli needs. That saves money, because extra fertilizer is money lost.

blocks.text: Broccoli nutrient deficiency questions

items.q: Why are my brokoli leaves turning yellow?
items.a: The most common cause is nitrogen deficiency: pale plants with orange to red edges on old leaves, and small, loose heads. If the young leaves turn yellow first instead, look at sulfur deficiency.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes nitrogen deficiency in broccoli?
items.a: Side dress urea or ammonium sulfate in split doses based on the soil test. For a quick green up, KAU suggests a urea spray at 10 grams per liter of water every 15 days for cole crops such as cabbage.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes boron deficiency in broccoli?
items.a: Delaware extension advises about 3 pounds of boron per acre in the fertilizer before planting for broccoli, or a spray of 1.0 to 1.5 pounds of Solubor per acre in plenty of water before heading if no boron went in the soil. For cole crops, KAU gives borax at about 10 kg per hectare in the soil or a 1 gram per liter spray.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes calcium deficiency in broccoli?
items.a: Keep the soil evenly moist. On acid soil, KAU suggests lime at about 250 kg per hectare when pH is 5.5 to 6, or about 840 kg per hectare in two doses when pH is 3.5 to 4.5.

items.q: How do I know which nutrient my brokoli lacks?
items.a: First look at where the change began, on the old leaves or the young ones, then at the color and the pattern. Next, confirm the broccoli nutrient deficiency with a soil test or a leaf test before you buy fertilizer.
